Subject: Air-gap deployment: MOP, network constraints, and next steps

Thanks again for the time today — wanted to capture the agreements and open questions so we have a single source of truth. Short recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps.

Key drivers / goals we heard
- Regulatory: state-level PHI residency + additional controls from your legal team drives the need for an air-gapped or one-way isolated deployment.
- Business goal: run inference for patient triage and chart summarization with sub-200ms internal latency for your clinician UI.
- Operational: 7+ years of audit log retention, HSM-backed key management, and strict change windows for software updates.

Confirmed pain points / constraints
- Compute must be isolated with no outbound internet egress from the inference cluster (only curated maintenance windows).
- No external telemetry or SaaS callbacks unless routed through an approved one-way mechanism.
- Patching must be performed via an internal bastion/air-gap process; firmware & OS patches are controlled by your infra team.
- Limited maintenance windows: 2 windows per month (2 hours each) for updates.

Open technical questions (please confirm quickly if possible)
1) Is outbound egress completely blocked at the datacenter edge, or is HTTP/HTTPS to an internal proxy allowed during maintenance windows?
2) Do you allow a one-way data-diode for telemetry (push only)?
3) Can we ship model binaries into a secure staging bucket inside your network via SFTP during maintenance windows, or must we use physical media?
4) Which port ranges are permitted for internal control-plane traffic (we currently expect 443 + a short range for health checks)?

Attachments I will send after this note: network_diagram_v2.pdf (your draft), a SOC2 evidence template (SOC2-evidence-request.xlsx), and a draft MOP (mop-draft.docx).

Immediate next steps (proposed)
- I: Schedule a 60-minute MOP review with your infra + security teams (please propose Wed/Thu this week).
- II: We will send a prefilled SOC2 evidence worksheet for your security team to validate.
- III: Ben & Marissa will produce a draft MOP for review before the call.

If the answers to the questions above are a hard no (e.g., no outbound egress even during maintenance), we will propose an architecture that uses on-prem-only model loading and a staged offline update process — we just need to confirm specifics to size the integration work.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with calendar options and the MOP draft.

Best,

Subject: Re: Air-gap deployment: MOP, network constraints, and next steps

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. A few answers and clarifications from our side (copied our security and infra SMEs).

Answers to your Qs:
1) Outbound egress: compute cannot reach the public internet at all. During maintenance windows we allow connections only to our internal update/proxy infrastructure (HTTPS to internal proxy IPs). No direct internet egress.
2) Data-diode: yes, we are comfortable with a one-way push for non-sensitive telemetry (metrics only) but PHI must never leave the site.
3) Model delivery: our preference is SFTP into a locked staging subnet during the maintenance window. Physical media is an option but adds procurement friction.
4) Ports: control-plane over 443 to the internal proxy; we can open a small ephemeral range (61000-61010) for health checks between nodes if needed — must be restricted to the internal subnet.

Additional notes:
- HSM: we have an on-site HSM (nCipher) that will host customer keys — you will need to integrate with our KMS gateway.
- Audit retention: legal requires immutable logs retained 7 years, with exportable CSVs on request.
- Change window: two maintenance windows: Tue 02:00–04:00 and Sat 01:00–03:00 local (PST).

I attached the network diagram draft we discussed (network_diagram_v2.pdf) — it shows the proposed isolated cluster, the staging SFTP subnet, and the proxy hop.

Stakeholders to include on the MOP review: Maya Singh (Security), Raj Patel (Infra, raj.patel@cedarcare.com), and our procurement lead Sara Lopez (sara.lopez@cedarcare.com).

If you can provide the MOP draft and SOC2 sheet ahead of a 60-minute call, we’ll have our SMEs review and come prepared with acceptance criteria.

—Jack
Jack Thomson
Director, Infrastructure & Security | CedarCare Health
jack.thomson@cedarcare.com
